summary: Count mission timeout from admission instead of consuming it during an after wait

replay.detail: Chained creation claims retain their timeout budget without arming a clock. Local transitions and replay arm the deadline from the accepted timestamp of the first after-run completion. Older creation deadlines are ignored for chained runs. Existing stores reconstruct admission clocks with indexed reads of after-run completion claims during the deadline-table migration; claims are not rewritten and no full history replay is required.

schema.detail: mission_run_deadlines.deadline_at_unix_ms becomes nullable to represent a retained, unarmed budget. Startup transactionally rebuilds this projection table, preserves its mutation and digest triggers, and updates only its digest rows. The smallclaims user_version is unchanged by this slice; no tables, indexes or claim fields are added. Replication exchanges add optional table-definition version metadata; peer status names definitions that cannot be compared. Legacy version is 1 and the admission deadline definition is 3.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and claim registry are unchanged. Existing optional creation deadline fields already allow null.

compatibility.detail: Timeout counts run time from admission. Direct runs arm at creation; after runs arm once on their first accepted after-run completion. Retries and revisions do not reset the clock. The deadline projection is definition version 3; peers advertise every digest and compare only matching table definitions. Signed log admission continues across versions. Legacy peers use their existing layout identity check to skip graph comparisons; modern peers retain comparisons for all unchanged definitions. Lagging older owners still apply creation-based timeout semantics until upgraded; deployments never wait for an offline member. TypeScript, Swift and stui mission deadline types are already optional and remain unchanged. If retained admission claims are unavailable but an after-step is already completed, the clock stays unknown and a runtime fault says the timeout is not armed. Duplicate completions and later generations cannot start a fresh budget; restore the original admission history and rebuild the projection, or cancel the run.

downtime.detail: First open transactionally rebuilds only the deadline table. It copies deadline rows and reads each chained run's indexed after-step and subject/kind completion claims, without scanning unrelated state claims. On the Linux shared build host in the debug test build, full Store::open took 0.371 seconds on a locally constructed synthetic fixture matching the online census: 5458 mission runs, 2368 deadline rows, 42 chained runs (21 admitted, 21 queued). It took 7.620 seconds on a synthetic 100000-deadline-row fixture with 20% chained, half admitted and half waiting; both are within the 30-second migration budget and online Linux unit startup limit of 90 seconds. Fixture construction and digest-oracle checks are excluded. These are synthetic fixture measurements, not production-store timings or a general performance result. Earlier indexed-plan measurements were 6.550 and 11.878 seconds; the original unconstrained join took 400.175 seconds. Later opens skip migration.

manual.detail: Operations must back up each store before its normal rolling upgrade, record the versioned deadline definition and that lagging older owners retain creation-based timeout semantics, and leave offline members to upgrade when they return. No capability barrier or wait for another machine is introduced. The table rebuild is not reversible in place. Before rolling, Operations must record: no rollback below this head. This release is forward-only. Deploy order matters: legacy members skip graph comparison across definition identities; current claims sync never repairs projections from a peer. Operations census on three online members found 5458 mission runs, 2368 deadline rows and 42 chained runs; Linux unit startup limit is 90 seconds, the online macOS plist has no configured start timeout, and the offline member was not measured.

recovery.detail: Prefer forward recovery, preserving accepted admission clocks. Binary rollback over the nullable table is unsupported: an actual older executable opens the database, then next_active_mission_deadline errors with Invalid column type Null at index: 0, name: deadline_at_unix_ms. The table rebuild is not reversible in place. Restoring a pre-upgrade backup requires an Operations recovery plan for all claims accepted since that backup; simply replacing the binary is insufficient. No rollback below this head: the older binary cannot read NULL deadlines (Invalid column type Null at index 0, deadline_at_unix_ms). Operations records this restriction before it rolls. A malformed accepted admission timestamp indicates corrupt ordering/provenance data and stops open with run-specific context before the deadline table is rebuilt; the transaction preserves the previous table and digest triggers. Restore trustworthy data instead of guessing a clock.
